propositions: When two bundles exist for the same ref, git ls-remote returns the ref at two SHAs, a fresh clone fails with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed', and push stalls because git-remote-s3 rejects writes while len(bundles)>1, creating an unclonable/unpushable store.

Upstream's git-remote-s3 Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is interactive-only (blocking input() on EOF) and discards the non-chosen head's unique events, causing data loss in an append-only event log where each divergent head carries distinct ticket commits.

The heal must use lossless multi-parent 2-parent iterated merges (never octopus, reusing rebar's existing sync._union_merge semantics) to fold N bundle heads while preserving all events, with the merged tip written before any original bundles are deleted to ensure crash-safety.

The doctor acquires the helper's per-ref lock (S3Remote.acquire_lock, conditional-put/60s-TTL) and enumerates bundles under the lock, then fetches each divergent head into scratch refs, merges them under rebar's write_lock, writes the merged bundle as a NEW object, deletes originals, and releases locks.

Push detection adds _is_multi_bundle predicate to identify the failure signatures ('multiple bundles exists on server', 'multiple updates for ref'), branches to heal_multi_bundle once (guarded by healed_once flag to prevent retry thrash), then retries the push.

The doctor routes all S3 access through the helper's own S3Remote/.s3 boto3 client (imported lazily behind require_s3_helper), adds no direct S3 SDK dependency to core rebar (boto3 transitive under optional [s3] extra), and never uses the forbidden merge=union driver.
